en.headline: Lam says existing laws already cover AI-aided crime
en.dek: The secretary for justice said dedicated AI statutes may follow if needed, as the Law Reform Commission studies deepfake pornography and scams.
body: Secretary for Justice Paul Lam said on Friday that the absence of dedicated artificial intelligence statutes does not leave a legal vacuum when the technology is used to commit crime.

Speaking after this week's Policy Address, which stressed that safe use of AI is as important as promoting the technology, Lam said existing, technology-neutral offences can already be applied. "So long as you're using some sort of instrument to facilitate the commission of a crime, that would constitute criminal conduct," he said.

The Law Reform Commission is examining whether new legislation is needed to tackle deepfake-generated pornographic images and deepfake-driven online scams, and is expected to submit a report to the government. Lam said the administration was deeply concerned about harm from AI misuse and would expedite legislation if intervention was judged necessary.

He added that legislation would be only one option and would have to be paired with other measures. A Department of Justice task force on minors' use of social media and their interactions with AI will be set up as soon as possible, and will also review legal liability for accidents caused by AI products.
Lam said the task force would work with other bureaux and study overseas practice before recommending an approach for Hong Kong.

zh.headline: 林定國：現行法例已可處理利用AI犯罪
zh.dek: 律政司司長表示，即使尚未有專門規管人工智能的法例，亦不代表出現真空；法律改革委員會正研究深偽色情及騙案。
body: 律政司司長林定國周五表示，現時未有專門規管人工智能的法例，並不代表當有人利用有關技術犯罪時出現法律真空。
他在本周《施政報告》強調發展與安全並重後指出，現行法例屬技術中立，只要有人利用工具協助犯罪，不論工具先進與否，都可構成刑事行為。他說，希望市民不要誤以為目前完全無法規管濫用人工智能作奸犯科。
法律改革委員會正研究是否需要新法例，打擊以深偽技術製作色情影像及進行網上詐騙，稍後會向政府提交報告。林定國說，當局高度關注濫用人工智能可能造成的傷害，若認為有需要介入，會加快立法。
他強調立法只是其中一個選項，必須配合其他措施。律政司將盡快成立專責小組，檢視未成年人使用社交媒體及與人工智能互動的情況，並研究人工智能產品引致意外的法律責任。
林定國表示，小組會與其他政策局合作，並參考海外做法，再提出適合香港的方案。
